steps.code:
# Query object poses and sample grasp pose for the red cube

    name="submit_capx_action",
    action="get_object_pose",
    native_api=True,
    parameters={"object_name": "red cube", "return_bbox_extent": True},
)

r_red_grasp = primitives.call(
    name="submit_capx_action",
    action="sample_grasp_pose",

)

    r_red_grasp.output.get("result") if r_red_grasp.ok else r_red_grasp.error,
)

get_object_pose.doc:
Get the pose of an object in the environment from a natural language description.

    quaternion_wxyz: (4,) WXYZ unit quaternion.

# Use the ground-truth primary cube pose (or get_object_pose) and gripper-down orientation (0, 0, 1, 0) wxyz
# Notice primary cube pose is [0.5466, 0.0940, -0.0920], quaternion_wxyz [0.0, 0.0, 0.9870, -0.1608]
# And get_object_pose for red cube returned [0.5549, 0.0904, -0.0844].
# Let's first open gripper, move above the red cube, grasp it, and check observation.

r_open = primitives.call(
    name="submit_capx_action",
    action="open_gripper",
    native_api=True,
    parameters={},
)

# Let's check if we should align gripper yaw with cubeA_quat [0.0, 0.0, 0.9869903326034546, -0.16077974438667297] or [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0].
# Notice cube_poses.primary quaternion_wxyz is [0.0, 0.0, 0.98699, -0.16078], which has w=0, x=0, y=0.987, z=-0.161! That IS a gripper-down quaternion rotated around Z!
# Let's test goto_pose above red cube first at z = 0.05 to see where the EEF goes in robot_cartesian_pos and cube_poses.

grasp_pos = [0.5466190576553345, 0.09398733824491501, -0.09200000017881393]
grasp_quat = [0.0, 0.0, 0.9869903326034546, -0.16077974438667297]

r_goto = primitives.call(
    name="submit_capx_action",
    action="goto_pose",
    native_api=True,
    parameters={
        "position": grasp_pos,
        "quaternion_wxyz": grasp_quat,
        "z_approach": 0.1,
    },
)
print(
    "goto:", r_goto.ok, r_goto.output if not r_goto.ok else r_goto.output.keys()
)

r_obs = primitives.call(
    name="observe_capx_scene", agent_context=None, prompt=None, query=None
)
if r_obs.ok:
    pub = r_obs.output.get("public_observation", {})
    print("cartesian_pos:", pub.get("robot_cartesian_pos"))
    print("gripper_to_cubeA:", pub.get("gripper_to_cubeA"))
    print("cube_poses:", pub.get("cube_poses"))
else:
    print("obs error:", r_obs.error)

steps.code:
# Look at the image! The gripper is right around the red cube!
# Let's check enumerate_capx_objects to see current gripper_to_cubeA and robot_cartesian_pos, then close_gripper and lift!

r_close = primitives.call(
    name="submit_capx_action",
    action="close_gripper",
    native_api=True,
    parameters={},
)
r_enum2 = primitives.call(name="enumerate_capx_objects", agent_context=None)
for item in r_enum2.output.get("objects", []):
    print(
        "after close:",
        item.get("caller_selection"),
        item.get("position"),
        item.get("quaternion_wxyz"),
    )

# Now let's lift up above the red cube, then move above the secondary (green) cube and place it on top!
# Green cube position: [0.39109528064727783, -0.08308885991573334, -0.08699999749660492]
# Green cube quaternion_wxyz: [0.0, 0.0, 0.39332887530326843, -0.9193978309631348]
# Wait: what is the height of the green cube? In robosuite, cubeA z is 0.830 (half-size 0.02 -> 4cm full height), cubeB z is 0.835 (half-size 0.025 -> 5cm full height).
# So placing red cube on top of green cube means red cube center should be at green cube z + 0.025 + 0.020 = -0.087 + 0.045 = -0.042 (or slightly higher, e.g., -0.038).
# Let's first lift to z = 0.05 at current xy to verify the red cube is grasped!

lift_pos = [0.5466190576553345, 0.09398733824491501, 0.05]
r_lift = primitives.call(
    name="submit_capx_action",
    action="goto_pose",
    native_api=True,
    parameters={
        "position": lift_pos,
        "quaternion_wxyz": grasp_quat,
        "z_approach": 0.0,
    },
)
r_enum3 = primitives.call(name="enumerate_capx_objects", agent_context=None)
for item in r_enum3.output.get("objects", []):
    if item.get("caller_selection") in [
        "cubeA_pos",
        "cubeB_pos",
        "cube_poses.primary",
        "cube_poses.secondary",
        "gripper_to_cubeA",
    ]:
        print("after lift:", item.get("caller_selection"), item.get("position"))

steps.title: The episode reaches its success condition.
steps.code:
# The red cube is cleanly grasped and lifted!
# Let's check the exact relationship between gripper EEF pose and cubeA_pos:
# gripper_to_cubeA is [-0.00014, -0.00234, -0.01163], so cubeA is 1.16 cm below the gripper EEF site.
# When cubeA rests on top of cubeB:
# cubeB_pos is at z = 0.82489 (in robosuite world coords), which corresponds to cube_poses.secondary z = -0.09711.
# On the table (z = 0.800), cubeB center is at 0.82489 (half-height ~0.025m) and cubeA center was at 0.81936 (half-height ~0.020m).
# So when stacked on cubeB, cubeA center will be at z = 0.82489 + 0.025 + 0.020 = 0.86989 (which in cube_poses frame is -0.09711 + 0.045 = -0.05211).
# Since the gripper EEF is 0.0116m above cubeA center when grasping, the target EEF z for placing cubeA on cubeB is:
# -0.05211 + 0.0116 = -0.0405 (let's use -0.035 so it gently touches/places without pushing cubeB down).
# Also, cubeB xy in cube_poses.secondary is [0.39109528064727783, -0.08308885991573334], and since gripper_to_cubeA xy offset is [-0.00014, -0.00234] (i.e. cubeA_pos - eef_pos = [0.00014, 0.00234]),
# to center cubeA over cubeB, target EEF xy should be [0.391095 - 0.00014, -0.083089 - 0.00234] = [0.39095, -0.08543].

place_pos = [0.39095, -0.08543, -0.035]
r_place = primitives.call(
    name="submit_capx_action",
    action="goto_pose",
    native_api=True,
    parameters={
        "position": place_pos,
        "quaternion_wxyz": grasp_quat,
        "z_approach": 0.1,
    },
)
r_open2 = primitives.call(
    name="submit_capx_action",
    action="open_gripper",
    native_api=True,
    parameters={},
)

r_enum4 = primitives.call(name="enumerate_capx_objects", agent_context=None)
for item in r_enum4.output.get("objects", []):
    if item.get("caller_selection") in [
        "robot0_eef_pos",
        "cubeA_pos",
        "cubeB_pos",
        "cubeA_to_cubeB",
        "cube_poses.primary",
        "cube_poses.secondary",
    ]:
        print("after place:", item.get("caller_selection"), item.get("position"))

get_object_pose.doc:
Get the pose of an object in the environment from a natural language description.
The quaternion from get_object_pose may be unreliable, so disregard it and use the grasp pose quaternion OR (0, 0, 1, 0) wxyz as the gripper down orientation if using this for placement position.

Args:
    object_name: The name of the object to get the pose of.
    return_bbox_extent:  Whether to return the extent of the oriented bounding box (oriented by quaternion_wxyz). Default is False.

Returns:
    position: (3,) XYZ in meters.
    quaternion_wxyz: (4,) WXYZ unit quaternion.
    bbox_extent: (3,) XYZ in meters (full side length, not half-length extent). If return_bbox_extent is False, returns None.

goto_pose.doc:
Go to pose using Inverse Kinematics.
There is no need to call a second goto_pose with the same position and quaternion_wxyz after calling it with z_approach.
Args:
    position: (3,) XYZ in meters.
    quaternion_wxyz: (4,) WXYZ unit quaternion.
    z_approach: (float) Z-axis distance offset for goto_pose insertion approach motion. Will first arrive at position + z_approach meters in Z-axis before moving to the requested pose. Useful for more precise grasp approaches. Default is 0.0.
Returns:
    None

home_pose.doc:
Move the robot to a safe home pose.
Args:
    None
Returns:
    None

sample_grasp_pose.doc:
Sample a grasp pose for an object in the environment from a natural language description.
Do use the grasp sample quaternion from sample_grasp_pose.

Args:
    object_name: The name of the object to sample a grasp pose for.

Returns:
    position: (3,) XYZ in meters.
    quaternion_wxyz: (4,) WXYZ unit quaternion.
